# Mahāsuññata Sutta (MN 122 (PTS MN iii 109))

**ID:** MN 122 (PTS MN iii 109)  
**Section:** Majjhimanikāya (mn)  
**Collection:** Sutta  
**Title (Pali):** Mahāsuññata Sutta  
**Title (English, from literature):** The Longer Discourse on Emptiness  
**PTS:** MN iii 109  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0203m.mul2.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0203m.mul2.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

No reliable discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus.

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Full parallels: MA 191 大空; D 291 མདོ་ཆེན་པོ་སྟོང་པ་ཉིད་ཆེན་པོ་ཞེས་བྱ་བ། (Mahāśūnyatā-nāma-mahāsūtra)
- Passage-level parallels: MN 139 (PTS MN iii 230) Araṇavibhaṅga Sutta

**Sources**

- [Fay and Bruckner 2011] Siegfried C.A. Fay and Ilse Maria Bruckner, eds., Buddhism as a Stronghold of Free Thinking (2011) — Note on Buddha admonishing Ānanda regarding excessive socializing and foregoing seclusion.
- [Underwood 1973] Frederic Bradley Underwood, Buddhist Insight: Nature and Function of Paññā in the Pāli Nikāyas (1973) — Record of translations by Robert Chalmers and Ñāṇamoli Thera.
- [Ray 1994] Reginald A. Ray, Buddhist Saints in India: A Study in Buddhist Values and Orientations (1994) — Analysis of inward emptiness, forest renunciants avoiding laity, and rejection of textual pursuits.
- [Peoples 2013] Dion Peoples, Buddhist Critical Thinking Skills (2013) — Discussions of monastic dweller discipline, solitude, and voidness of distractions.
- [Shonin et al. 2015] Edo Shonin, William Van Gordon, and Nirbhay N. Singh, eds., Buddhist Foundations of Mindfulness (2015) — Treatment of emptiness meditation, vipassanā, and giving attention to voidness.
- [Ganeri 2018] Jonardon Ganeri, Attention, Not Self (2018) — Reference to Ñāṇamoli's translation of the sutta with commentary from the Papañcasūdanī.
- [Choong 1999] Choong Mun-keat, The Notion of Emptiness in Early Buddhism (1999) — Identification of Chinese counterpart MĀ 191 (Dàkōng jīng), doctrinal overview of emptiness, and the three aṅgas.
- [Fagernes 1992] Proceedings of the 6th Seminar of the International Association for Tibetan Studies (Fagernes, 1992) — Tibetan title in the Kanjur (mDo chen po ston pa ñid chen po žes bya ba) matching MN 122.
- [Anālayo 2003] Bhikkhu Anālayo, Satipaṭṭhāna: The Direct Path to Realization (2003) — Treatment of clear knowing (sampajañña) regarding suitable speech and bodily postures.
- [Meisig 2010] Konrad Meisig, ed., Translating Buddhist Chinese: Problems and Prospects (2010) — Comparative analysis of the conceit 'I am' across Pali, Chinese, and Tibetan versions, and discussion of the three aṅgas.
